title: LP1 column balance after searching six widths
question: Is the minimum normalized column imbalance unusually low after searching widths 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64?
summary: Width 2 minimizes normalized imbalance. Matching that six-width search in every unrestricted shuffle gives p=0.12072; this is not an adjustment of the smallest fixed-width p-value.

scope.representation: Archived ciphertext runes, headings and interrupting F retained. Join slash and newline wraps and consecutive pages within a section. Rune runs with internal apostrophes form one word; apostrophes count zero runes. Other non-runes delimit words. Never merge sections.
scope.procedure: Keep the original four-section word order. For each width 2,4,8,16,32,64, assign word i to column i modulo width without padding. Calculate weighted column imbalance divided by its exact unrestricted-permutation expectation; select the minimum R. Repeat all six widths in every shuffled control.
scope.parameters: 49,999 unrestricted fresh-copy shuffles; Python Random seed 330146; exact rational comparisons; lower tail with ties; plus-one correction; threshold 0.05. Partial final rows retained. Original width-16 result and qualitative width observations known before this protocol.
scope.exclusions: Other widths; section reordering; start rotations; padding; within-section or sentence-preserving nulls; choosing the smallest fixed-width p-value; original exploratory multiplicity; authorial intent; decryption.

finding: The observed minimum R is 4167/245948 at width 2. Of 49,999 controls, 6,035 have a minimum no greater; plus-one estimate 0.12072.
limitations: Calibrates minimum R over six declared widths, not selection of the smallest fixed-width p-value or all historical exploration. Unrestricted shuffles do not preserve sentences or section distributions. No intent or decryption claim; human review pending.
next_steps: Other width sets or selecting a calibrated tail require separate frozen procedures and matched controls.
